question: The atomic mass of an atom is primarily determined by the number of:
solution:
The correct answer is __**nucleons**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The atomic mass of an atom is primarily determined by the total number of **nucleons** (protons and neutrons).
 
• Protons and neutrons are located in the nucleus of an atom and contribute most of the mass, as electrons have negligible mass.
 
• The mass number, which is approximately equal to the atomic mass, is the sum of the number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus.
 
• For example, Carbon-12 has 6 protons and 6 neutrons, giving it a mass number of 12.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Protons**:

 
 
• Positively charged particles located in the nucleus of an atom.
 
• The number of protons defines the atomic number and the element itself.
 
 
 
• **Neutrons**:
 
 
• Neutral particles located in the nucleus of an atom.
 
• Neutrons contribute to the stability of the nucleus.
 
 
 
• **Electrons**:
 
 
• Negatively charged particles that orbit the nucleus.
 
• Electrons have a much smaller mass compared to protons and neutrons.
 
 
 
• **Isotopes**:
 
 
• Atoms of the same element with the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.
 
• Isotopes have different mass numbers but the same chemical properties.
